title: Assessing the Practical Deployment of Thermally Activated Building Envelopes: A Six-Dimensional Review and Design Framework
content: Thermally activated building envelopes combine embedded heat exchange with building thermal mass, but component-level improvements do not necessarily translate into practical benefits. This critical review examines an existing collection of 84 documentary records, consolidated into 83 analytical units after version checking. Content is assessed across performance effectiveness, technical feasibility, engineering compatibility, operational robustness, economic viability, and institutional compatibility. Within this collection, 52 units do not address economic viability and 46 do not address institutional compatibility. These frequencies describe content coverage rather than evidence quality. Reported component heat-flow reductions, building load reductions, system energy savings, and cost benefits have different boundaries and cannot be treated as equivalent. Thermal-barrier, base-load conditioning, and storage functions consequently require separate statements of capability and responsibility. An assessment framework links envelope components, building spaces, and energy systems through the six dimensions. A seven-stage process translates the literature into project inputs, functional allocation, coordinated selection, system configuration, operational assessment, verification and handover, and monitoring feedback. The framework supports early-stage screening and interdisciplinary design, while its project-specific applicability requires further verification.
